problems_discovered: Extreme class imbalance: Normal constitutes 86.88% of data, whereas Oral Cancer is only 0.81% (20 images total).
High validation instability risk for Oral Cancer: validation set contains only 2 images from 2 patients. A single classification error flips validation recall between 50% and 100%.
Limited statistical power in test set for Oral Cancer: test set contains only 5 images from 5 patients. One false negative lowers sensitivity by 20 percentage points.

Split algorithm is patient-level but NOT class-aware: splitting is an unstratified patient shuffle. The presence of all four classes in val and test was fortunate for seed 42 rather than mathematically guaranteed.

conclusion.reason: The split strictly succeeds at preventing patient-level data leakage (0 patient overlap across all sets) and fortuitously achieves representation of all 4 classes in train, validation, and test. However, the extreme scarcity of Oral Cancer (only 2 validation images, 5 test images) coupled with an unstratified patient split creates significant risk of validation metric volatility and wide test confidence intervals.
conclusion.next_recommended_step: Before training, upgrade patient_level_split() to a patient-level stratified grouping (StratifiedGroupKFold or greedy patient-stratification) to guarantee balanced cross-split representation of rare classes, and evaluate whether 4-class or 3-class framing (Normal/Healthy vs OPMD vs OSCC) with class-weighted loss should be adopted.
